## Project Overview

Super Soakerz was a student-led car window washing business created as part of a marketing course at Cal Poly Pomona. The goal of the project was to build a service brand from scratch, promote it on campus, and evaluate real customer response.

The campaign focused on convenience, affordability, and visibility within a student commuter environment.

## Marketing Strategy

The primary target market included Cal Poly Pomona commuter students ages 18 to 25 who needed a quick and affordable service on campus.

The brand was positioned as:

- Student-run  
- Affordable  
- Eco-friendly  
- Convenient for commuter students  

The marketing approach focused on in-person promotion, visual branding, and simple messaging to build awareness and trust.

## Campaign Execution

The team promoted the service through campus outreach, physical signage, and peer-to-peer communication.

Visual branding included bright colors and easy-to-understand messaging. Promotional materials emphasized value, speed, and convenience. The campaign also used before-and-after visuals to show service quality and build credibility.

## Analytics and Results

### Key Performance Metrics

```{r}
library(gt)

kpi <- data.frame(
  Metric = c(
    "Total Customers Served",
    "Basic Package Sales",
    "Premium Package Sales",
    "Total Revenue",
    "Total Profit"
  ),
  Value = c(
    "18",
    "9",
    "9",
    "$63",
    "$49.50"
  )
)

gt(kpi) |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Super Soakerz Campaign Results",
    subtitle = "Summary of customers, sales, revenue, and profit"
  )
```
